name: Bodegas Muga Rioja Prado Enea Gran Reserva 2010
text:
## Bodegas Muga Rioja Prado Enea Gran Reserva 2010

**The story.** Bodegas Muga, in [Haro](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Bodegas+Muga,+Haro,+La+Rioja,+Spain&t=k), the historic wine town of [Rioja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rioja_DOCa) Alta, is one of the great traditional Rioja houses; Wine Advocate's Luis Gutiérrez notes that its fermentation vats are built by Muga's own coopers ([Berry Bros. & Rudd](https://us.bbr.com/collections/region-spain-rioja-wine/products/2010-prado-enea-gran-reserva-bodegas-muga-rioja-spain)).

**The wine: Prado Enea.** Prado Enea is Muga's Gran Reserva and an icon of Rioja. It comes from cool, high vineyards at 550 to 700 metres in the north-west of [Rioja Alta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rioja_DOCa), in Sajazarra, Cellorigo and Fonzaleche, on clay-limestone and alluvial soils; its grapes are always the last in the appellation to be picked. Hand-picked with a double selection, it ferments in oak vats with gentle pump-overs and 14 to 16 days of maceration, ages at least 36 months in mostly French oak barrels, is fined with fresh egg whites and then rests at least 36 more months in bottle ([Bodegas Muga](https://www.bodegasmuga.com/prado-enea-gran-reserva/), in Spanish). Gutiérrez gives the blend as about 70% [Tempranillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempranillo), 20% [Garnacha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) and 10% Mazuelo and [Graciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graciano); it is bottled only every two or three years (2007 and 2008 were skipped), and Muga delays the malolactic fermentation until spring by opening the winery windows to let the cold in ([Berry Bros. & Rudd](https://us.bbr.com/collections/region-spain-rioja-wine/products/2010-prado-enea-gran-reserva-bodegas-muga-rioja-spain)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Rioja and Ribera del Duero vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/rioja-and-ribera-del-duero) calls 2010 good in Rioja, better than 2009, and exceptional in Ribera del Duero. Gutiérrez called 2010 "one of the more balanced vintages of recent times". About 90,000 bottles were made.

**What the critics say for 2010.** As listed by [Berry Bros. & Rudd](https://us.bbr.com/collections/region-spain-rioja-wine/products/2010-prado-enea-gran-reserva-bodegas-muga-rioja-spain):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 97** (Luis Gutiérrez, February 2018). "The most classical among the wines in the portfolio", like the wines of yesteryear "but with today's knowledge". Never a dark wine; subtle and elegant on the nose, with "unbelievable elegance and harmony" on the palate, very fine tannins and "phenomenal" length. Medium-bodied, with perfect ripeness; it should have a very long life.
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 97** (Joaquín Hidalgo, December 2023). A mature wine with herbs and sour cherry, dried flowers, plums and a subtle layer of cigar box; dry, silky and juicy, with delicate tannins.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.2** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2042. Classic Gran Reserva like this is only now in its stride: sour cherry, dried flowers, cigar box, leather and spice. Decant gently, mainly for sediment, and serve at 16 to 17°C.

**Food.** Rioja's own: roast lamb (*cordero asado*), lamb chops grilled over vine cuttings, *chuletón* steak, roast suckling pig, or aged Manchego and Idiazabal.

**Value and where to buy.** Prado Enea is easy to find here: BC Liquor has the 2015 at $105.99, BSW Liquor the 2016 at $115 and ZYN the 2016 at $108. Muga's Reserva (from $28.99) and Selección Especial (about $54) are also widely stocked.

**From the history books**
- **Bottled only in great years.** Prado Enea is bottled only every two or three years; after 2010 came 2011, a small 2014 and 2015 ([Berry Bros. & Rudd](https://us.bbr.com/collections/region-spain-rioja-wine/products/2010-prado-enea-gran-reserva-bodegas-muga-rioja-spain)).

**Curious details**
- **Cold windows.** Muga opens the winery windows in winter so the cold delays the malolactic fermentation until spring ([Berry Bros. & Rudd](https://us.bbr.com/collections/region-spain-rioja-wine/products/2010-prado-enea-gran-reserva-bodegas-muga-rioja-spain)).
- **Egg whites.** The wine is still clarified the old way, with fresh egg whites ([Bodegas Muga](https://www.bodegasmuga.com/prado-enea-gran-reserva/)).
